narrative: I replayed the banked 33-action level-1 prefix and used only rendered grids, frame.levels_completed, and observed action outcomes. I recovered the prior attempt's four-placement route from its permitted action/frame transcript, reproduced its immediate post-drop checks, and tested both delayed-drop chaining and an alternate source order. Delaying a drop until the mover touched the next source was mechanically valid but saved no timer cells because dropping and re-picking still required two ticks; alternate directional inputs repositioned the orientation marker without changing the mover's source route. The best continuous run again confirmed four explicit placements before forced timer expiry, while the final clean run confirmed three placements and left two sources with only 16 timer cells. I stopped at 296 of 350 env.step calls because a forced expiry plus a new attempt would leave fewer than 39 calls, below the observed minimum needed for even three placements. levels_completed never exceeded 1, so no winning sequence existed to send through reproduce().
